content.value_statement: Reinforcement learning projects need careful setup for training speed, environment design, and policy structure. This skill gives PufferLib workflows, templates, and reference guidance for practical implementation.
actual_capabilities: Plan PPO training workflows with PuffeRL and common hyperparameters.
Create custom single-agent and multi-agent PufferEnv environments.
Choose vectorization settings for parallel simulation and throughput.
Design PyTorch policies for vector, image, recurrent, and multi-agent observations.
Integrate Gymnasium, PettingZoo, Atari, Procgen, Minigrid, and related environments.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates, not a complete trained model.
Users still need local PufferLib, PyTorch, and environment dependencies.
Performance claims depend on hardware, environment cost, and vectorization settings.
External experiment loggers may require user-provided service credentials.

use_cases.title: Train Existing Benchmarks
use_cases.description: Configure PPO training for Ocean, Procgen, Atari, Gymnasium, or PettingZoo environments.

use_cases.title: Build Custom Environments
use_cases.description: Use PufferEnv patterns to define observations, actions, rewards, resets, and multi-agent behavior.

use_cases.title: Improve Training Throughput
use_cases.description: Tune vectorization, worker counts, batch sizes, and profiling steps for faster RL experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Start PPO Training
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an existing environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me train a PufferLib PPO agent on [environment]. Include setup, key parameters, logging, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a PufferEnv
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PufferEnv for [task]. Define observations, actions, rewards, termination logic, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Vectorization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PufferLib training setup. Recommend vectorization, worker, batch, and profiling changes for higher steps per second.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Agent Training
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-agent PufferLib plan for [scenario]. Cover environment API, shared policies, logging, scaling, and debugging.

output_examples.input: Train a Procgen CoinRun PPO agent with PufferLib.
output: Environment setup with recommended parallel environment counts.
A training workflow covering policy selection, logging, checkpoints, and evaluation.
Validation steps for rewards, observations, throughput, and saved models.
A PufferEnv design with per-agent observations, discrete actions, and shared episode state.
Reward shaping guidance for distance, goal completion, and time limits.
A testing checklist for reset behavior, step outputs, and multi-agent done flags.

output_examples.input: My RL training is slower than expected.
output: A bottleneck review covering environment cost, worker counts, batch size, and device use.
A prioritized tuning plan for vectorization, profiling, and optional native optimization.

best_practices: Validate observation and action spaces before scaling training runs.
Profile steps per second early and after each optimization change.
Start with proven environments before building custom environment logic.
anti_patterns: Do not tune many hyperparameters before confirming environment correctness.
Do not scale workers without measuring whether the environment or policy is the bottleneck.
Do not add external loggers until credentials and project names are configured intentionally.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps build, train, integrate, and optimize reinforcement learning workflows with PufferLib.

faq.question: Does it train models automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates that users run in their own environment.

faq.question: Which RL frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: It covers PufferLib Ocean, Gymnasium, PettingZoo, Atari, Procgen, Minigrid, and related integrations.

faq.question: Can it help with multi-agent tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes multi-agent environment patterns, shared policy guidance, and PettingZoo integration notes.

faq.question: Does it require GPUs?
faq.answer: No. CPU training is possible, but GPU acceleration can improve policy training throughput.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare the target environment, installed dependencies, hardware constraints, and success metrics for the experiment.
